name: Nicephorus Phocas Reconquests, Cilicia and Cyprus
summary: Emperor Nicephorus II Phocas (r. 963-969) leads a series of brilliant military campaigns that reconquer Cilicia (964-965), Cyprus (965), and finally Antioch (969) from the Hamdanid emirate. The campaigns represent the greatest Byzantine territorial expansion since Justinian and demonstrate that the Macedonian dynasty's military reforms have created a formidable offensive force. Nicephorus is assassinated in 969 by his nephew John Tzimiskes, but the gains are permanent.

_quarry.structural_significance: The reconquest of Antioch (lost since 637) restores Byzantine control over Syria and shifts the military frontier east; these gains create the overextension that the Battle of Manzikert (1071) fatally exposes; the eastern campaigns also exhaust the military treasury and contribute to the civilian-military factional conflict that weakens the Byzantine state in the 11th century
